facts.fact: Adwave states that CPMs for TV advertising are often 20-40% lower during non-holiday periods.
facts.quote: CPMs (the cost to reach 1,000 viewers) are often 20-40% lower during non-holiday periods.

facts.fact: Adwave states that customers can create a professional TV commercial and start reaching local customers for as little as $30 a day.
facts.quote: you can create a professional TV commercial and start reaching local customers for as little as $30 a day.

facts.fact: Adwave gives an illustrative example in which a $100 slow-season TV campaign might deliver the same reach as a $150 campaign during peak season; this is a hypothetical example, not measured data.
facts.quote: A $100 campaign during your slow season might deliver the same reach as a $150 campaign during peak.

facts.fact: Adwave defines CPM as cost per thousand impressions.
facts.quote: Less competition for ad inventory means lower CPMs (cost per thousand impressions).

facts.fact: Adwave lists the wedding industry's slow months as January through March and November.
Adwave states that many engagements happen in December, which it cites as a reason for wedding vendors to advertise during that period.
facts.quote: Engagement season advertising (many engagements happen in December)

facts.fact: Adwave offers a 'Buy $50, get $10 free' gift card promotion as an example of an off-season offer; this is an example offer, not a fixed program.
facts.quote: "Buy $50, get $10 free" promotions during slow periods seed future visits.

facts.fact: The page advises businesses to start increasing marketing investment four to six weeks before they expect demand to rise.
facts.quote: Start increasing marketing investment four to six weeks before you expect demand to rise.
